# E133 -- Dropbox

## Metadata
- **Brand**: Dropbox
- **Industry**: Cloud Storage / SaaS / Technology
- **Document**: Dropbox Brand Guidelines
- **Year**: 2017 (August 26, 2017)
- **Pages**: 23
- **Designer/Agency**: Not credited (internal brand team; coincides with the Collins-led 2017 rebrand era)

## Brand Strategy
- No dedicated brand strategy section. This is a tactical/execution-focused guidelines document rather than a strategy-led brand book.
- **Structure**: 5 sections -- Logo/Glyph Guidelines & Don'ts, Color Don'ts, Typography Don'ts, Motion Guidelines, Sample Banner Design & PSD.

## Logo
- **Glyph**: The iconic Dropbox open-box diamond shape (four overlapping diamond/rhombus forms) in Dropbox Blue.
- **Secondary glyph**: A dotted circular pattern (appears alongside the classic box on the cover) -- likely part of the 2017 rebrand's expanded visual system.
- **Lockup**: Glyph + "Dropbox" wordmark in a horizontal arrangement, left-aligned. Logo always positioned at corners or center-edge positions on layouts.
- **Logo placement**: 6 approved positions demonstrated on landscape and portrait templates -- top-left, top-right, center-left, center-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
- **Logo don'ts** (10 rules): Do not rotate glyph, do not deconstruct glyph, do not stretch glyph, do not fill in glyph (with imagery/patterns), do not color logotype, do not use wrong colors, do not use gradients, do not center lockup, do not outline glyph or wordmark.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface**: Sharp Grotesk (Sharp Type foundry) -- "the primary brand typeface for Dropbox."
- **Usage**: Used for all display text and information for all communications.
- **Weights** (3 primary): Book 22, Medium 22, Semibold 22 -- all in roman (no italic specified).
- **Style**: Modern geometric grotesque with clean, rounded forms. Large x-height, distinctive character.
- **Typography don'ts**: Dedicated section (not directly sampled but referenced in TOC).

## Color
- **Primary**: Dropbox Blue (the signature bright blue, approximately #0061FF) -- used for cover background and glyph.
- **Color don'ts** (10 rules): Do not use gradients, do not use non-brand colors, do not use color effects, do not use black as background with brand colors, do not use non-system color pairings, do not use black on dark colors, do not use high-contrast colors (e.g., red background), do not use one color for both logo and glyph, do not use white glyph with colored wordmark, do not use DBX Blue with non-system colors.
- **Implication**: Strict color system with approved pairings; black backgrounds explicitly prohibited with brand color elements.

## Graphics
- **Dotted pattern**: Circular dot-cluster motif visible on cover (part of the 2017 visual system expansion beyond the classic box).
- **Motion guidelines**: Dedicated section (Chapter 4) suggests animated brand assets with specific motion principles.

## Photography
- Not covered in this document.

## Applications
- **Sample Banner Design & PSD**: Chapter 5 provides template banner designs with source PSD files -- practical, production-ready assets for partners/advertisers.
- **Motion Guidelines**: Chapter 4 covers animated/motion applications.

## Tone of Voice
- Not covered in this document.

## Outliers
- Heavily "don'ts"-focused document -- 3 of 5 sections are explicitly about what NOT to do (Logo Don'ts, Color Don'ts, Typography Don'ts). This suggests it was created as a partner/third-party compliance tool rather than an internal creative guide.
- The inclusion of PSD source files indicates this was likely distributed to advertising partners or co-marketing stakeholders.
- Notably compact (23 pages) for a major tech brand -- this is a subset/extract of a larger brand system, not the complete guidelines.
- The 2017 date places this during Dropbox's significant Collins-designed rebrand, but this document captures only the tactical rules, not the creative vision.
- PDF has internal structural errors (corrupted xref table) but renders successfully.

## Quality Score
- **2/5** -- Functional but limited partner-facing compliance document. Strong on logo and color misuse prevention (20+ don't examples across two sections). Sharp Grotesk typography well-specified. However, lacks any brand strategy, tone of voice, photography, or creative direction. No color values provided (only misuse examples). No positive examples of correct application beyond logo placement. Serves a narrow purpose as a third-party usage guide rather than a comprehensive brand resource.
